transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really hope I'm not taking up a spot from someone who needs it more, but... um... I guess I'm here because things have gotten a little overwhelming lately. 

I know this is probably a terrible thing to say right off the bat, and I'm sorry to even bring it up, but... I just keep thinking that it might be better if I just didn't wake up in the morning. It's embarrassing to admit that out loud. It's just... I've made things so hard for my family, and I've really let down my flooring crew at work, too. Sometimes I honestly feel like dying would just be the fair punishment for what I've done to all of them. 

I know I shouldn't think that way, and I really am trying to be better about it. I hope it's okay that I came in to talk about this... is that the sort of thing you can help with?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, well... I guess it's been a while now. Probably about a year and five months? I'm sorry, I should probably know the exact date, but... it started right around the time my husband hurt his back. He's been mostly housebound since then, and... well, I just haven't been handling it very well, which is completely my fault. I should be stronger for him. I hope that's the kind of timeline you were looking for? I can try to be more specific if you need me to be.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Oh, um... I really try to keep up with things, I promise I do. I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or giving up. But... well, I used to do a lot. I'd paint, cook these big meals, go for a run before my flooring jobs, and I even used to show up for theater rehearsals. 

But lately... and I'm really sorry to admit this, because it sounds terrible... those things just feel like chores now. Almost like they're from somebody else's life? And I just... I don't really care if I miss them anymore. I know I should, and I'm trying to care, I really am. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it the right way.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened?

Um... yes. Yes, I do. I know I probably shouldn't dwell on things, and I really try to just look on the bright side, but... I just feel so awful about everything. 

I don't want to sound dramatic, but... I just keep thinking that I'm the reason my husband's back got worse. And I'm the reason my crew lost out on jobs. It's like... I don't know, like I've just messed up clients' homes and poisoned everything I've touched. I really try to be a good person, I promise, but sometimes I just feel like I completely deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I shouldn't be so negative. Is it normal to feel that way? I hope I'm not overreacting.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how you're moving, like feeling slowed down or restless?

Um... well, I really try to push through it, I promise. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, because I know installing tile is a physical job and I should be used to it by now. But... yes, I guess I have been feeling a lot slower lately. 

It's just... by the time I carry even one box of tile, or honestly, even if I just sit down to answer a couple of client messages... my body just feels like wet cement. And my head gets so tired that I just can't make simple decisions anymore. 

I feel so bad about it, because I know I need to be more productive, and I really am trying to get my stamina back up so I don't let anyone else down. Is that what you meant by feeling slowed down? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you typically feel worse in the morning?

Um... morning? I don't know if I'd say I feel worse then, specifically. I really try to wake up with a good attitude, I promise. I try to tell myself it's a new day and I'm going to do better. 

I guess I haven't really noticed a difference between the morning and the rest of the day. It just sort of... all feels the same right now? I hope that's okay. I know sometimes people have a specific time they feel bad, but I just haven't really kept track of it like that. Is that a bad thing? I can start paying more attention to the time of day if that would help you.
Have you made any plans to act on those thoughts about not waking up in the morning?

Um... no, no, I haven't made any plans. I promise I wouldn't do anything like that. I know it sounds terrible that I even think about it, and I really don't want to upset you or anyone else. 

It's just... well, that's actually why I came in. I just keep having these thoughts that... that it would be better if I just didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes... I don't know, sometimes it just feels like dying would be the only fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's a horrible thing to say. I really am trying to be stronger than this. I know I shouldn't think that way, and I'm really hoping you can help me fix it so I can be normal again. Is it okay that I told you that? I just wanted to be honest with you.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?

Um... well... I know this probably sounds really strange, and I hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying it. I really hesitate to even bring it up because I know it sounds bad, but I want to be a good patient and give you all the information you need. 

Sometimes... and it's not all the time, I promise... but sometimes I hear a man's voice. It usually happens when I'm at a job site, or even just standing in my own kitchen. It sounds like he's right behind me, just clear as day, like someone is actually standing right there. He says things like, "You missed it," or "Everyone knows." 

I always turn around right away to apologize or see who it is, but... there's never anyone there. I know it must just be my mind playing tricks on me because I'm so stressed and tired. I really try to just ignore it and keep working. I hope it's okay that I shared that with you. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
How often do you hear the man's voice?

Um... I'm really not sure exactly. I'm so sorry, I know I should probably have a better answer for you. 

It's definitely not constantly, I promise you that. I just... I try so hard to block it out and focus on my work, you know? Just keep my head down, lay the flooring, and make sure everything looks right for the clients. Because I really try to ignore it, I guess I just haven't kept a tally of how often it actually happens. 

I really hope it's not frustrating for you that I don't have an exact number. Would you like me to start writing it down when it happens? I can definitely start keeping a log if it makes your job easier and helps us fix this.
Does the man's voice you hear ever tell you to do something or give you commands?

Oh, no, no... I promise it doesn't do that. It never tells me to do anything or gives me orders. I really hope that's a good sign? 

Like I was saying a minute ago, it's really just... just those little passing comments, like "You missed it" or "Everyone knows." It always just sounds like he's standing right behind me making an observation, but he never, ever tells me to do anything bad, I swear. I would definitely tell you if he did, because I really want to be completely honest with you. 

Is it... is it better that he doesn't tell me to do things? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can fix this.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss or gain recently?

Um... well, I really hope you don't think I'm neglecting my health or anything. I know I'm supposed to be taking good care of myself... but I guess I have lost a little bit of weight. I'm really not trying to, I promise! 

It's just... most days, I just sort of forget to eat until it's really late. And then when I finally do try to have something, I'll take a few bites and just feel kind of sick to my stomach. My work pants have actually gotten pretty loose on me lately because of it. 

I hope that's not a bad thing? I can definitely try harder to force myself to eat more during the day if you want me to. I just want to make sure I'm doing whatever you think is best. Is that something I should be worried about?
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in activities?

Um... yes. I really hope you don't judge me for this, because I know I should be stronger and handle things better. But... yeah, it's been a lot longer than two weeks. 

I've been feeling this way for... gosh, about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband got injured. I really tried to keep a positive attitude for him, I promise I did. I didn't want to be a burden when he was already going through so much. But it just got so heavy, and I stopped caring about things I used to enjoy. 

I feel so guilty admitting that it's been going on for that long without me fixing it. Is it... is it normal for it to last that long after something like that happens? I just really want you to know I've been trying my best to push through it.
Do you often feel restless or have an intense need to move around?

Um... no, I don't think I do. I really hope that's okay? I mean, I don't get that feeling where I have to pace or anything like that. 

With my job installing flooring and tile, I'm usually just so exhausted by the time I get home that I just want to sit still. I hope I'm not being too inactive... I can definitely try to get up and move around more if you think I should be doing that? I really don't mind trying if it would help. But no, I don't really feel restless or anything. Is... is that a good sign?
Do you hear the man's voice at the same time every day?

Um... no, not really at the same time. I hope it's okay that I can't give you a specific schedule for it. I really try to ignore it, I promise I do. 

It just sort of happens randomly... like when I'm at a job site working on a floor, or even just standing in my own kitchen. I'll hear this man's voice right behind me, clear as day, like he's standing right over my shoulder. He says things like, 'You missed it,' or... or 'Everyone knows.' 

I know it probably sounds crazy, and I'm so sorry, I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind. But it sounds so real that I always turn around to apologize or see who it is, and... nobody's ever there. 

I know I shouldn't let it bother me, and I'm really trying to just focus on my work when it happens. Is... is it really bad that I'm hearing that? I can try harder to tune it out if you think that would be better.
Do you feel like you're a burden to your family and friends most of the time?

Um... yes, I do. I really hate to admit it, because I know I should be more positive and stop feeling sorry for myself. I hope you don't think I'm just looking for pity or anything. 

But... yeah, I feel like a huge burden. I just... I keep thinking that I'm the reason my husband got worse after his injury. Like if I had just been a better wife, he wouldn't be struggling so much. And... and at work, I feel like I'm the reason the crew lost out on some jobs. I just feel like I've messed up clients' homes, even when they say the tile looks fine. 

I don't know, I just... I feel like I poison everything I touch. Like I just ruin things for everyone around me, and I deserve whatever bad things happen to me because of it. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's a terrible way to think. I really try to keep those thoughts to myself so I don't drag anyone else down. Is it... is it normal to feel that guilty all the time? I promise I'm trying to be better about it.
Do you feel like your depression is mildly, moderately, or severely interfering with your daily life?

Um... I guess I would have to say it's severely interfering. I'm really sorry to admit that, I know I should be handling things better. I hope you don't think I'm just giving up or being weak.

It's just... I actually had to stop leading the flooring installations. I really tried to keep going, I promise I did, but I just couldn't safely manage the crew anymore, or deal with the clients and make the right decisions for the jobs. I just felt so overwhelmed and confused, and I was so scared I was going to ruin the work or put someone at risk. 

My apprentice and my husband actually had to start stepping in to take over for me before I messed everything up. I feel terrible that they had to do that, making more work for them... I really want to get back to pulling my own weight. Is it... is it okay that I stepped back from leading for a little while? I'm really hoping I can fix this and get back to normal soon.
Have you ever thought about how you would carry out those thoughts of not waking up in the morning?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't have a specific plan or anything like that. I hope that's the right answer, I don't want to worry you or make you think I'm, you know, a danger or something. I really try not to dwell on it.

It's just... I came in today because I do keep having those thoughts. Like, I just keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up in the morning. And... sometimes I just feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. Like it's what I deserve for messing everything up. 

But I promise I haven't actually planned anything out. I know it's awful to even think those things, and I'm really trying to push them away. Is it... does that make sense? I really am trying to be better, I promise.
Have you ever thought about how you would carry out those thoughts of not waking up in a specific way?

Oh, um... I'm sorry if I wasn't clear just a second ago. I really haven't thought about a specific way to do it, I promise. I hope you believe me, I'm really not trying to hide anything from you. 

It's just like I mentioned... I came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up. And... sometimes I just feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. Like it's the only way to make up for the burden I've been. But I haven't actually sat down and figured out a specific way to make that happen. 

I'm really trying not to let it get to that point, which is why I wanted to tell you about it. I hope it's okay that I don't have a plan? I just want to do whatever I'm supposed to do to fix this and stop being such a problem for everyone.
Would you say your feelings of depression are improving, staying the same, or getting worse over time?

Um... I guess I would have to say it's staying the same, or maybe getting a little worse? I'm sorry, I know I should be making progress by now. I really am trying to stay positive, I promise. 

It's just... this heavy feeling, the depression... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband had his injury. I really thought I could just push through it and be strong for him, but it just hasn't lifted. I hope you don't think I'm not trying hard enough to get better. Is it... is it normal for it to last this long? I really want to be doing the right things to get past this.
Would you describe your current depressive feelings as mild, moderate, or severe?

Um... I guess maybe moderate? Or... maybe a little more than that? I don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much. I mean, it's pretty heavy, so I suppose it could be severe, but I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or not trying to fight it. 

I really am trying my best to handle it. I hope it doesn't make me sound weak if I say it feels pretty severe right now. Does that... does that sound like the right way to describe it, given how long it's been going on? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I can get better.
